newsitem.title: UK: Strong sterling hits Sedgwick Q1 profits.
newsitem.headline: Strong sterling hits Sedgwick Q1 profits.

text.p: The strength of the British pound knocked off 3.4 million pounds ($5.5 million) from pre-tax profits of insurance broker Sedgwick Group Plc in the first three months of the current financial year.
Sedgwick said its pre-tax profits slipped slightly to 43.5 million pounds from 45.3 million in the previous year as it maintained an earnings per share of 5.5 pence a share.
On a constant exchange rate the group's pre-tax profits would have shown a rise of four percent while its EPS would have risen eight percent.

Sedgwick's chairman Sax Riley, however, remained confident on the company's performance saying it would continue to look for "new intiatives aimed at additional profit improvement and cost containment".
"These results are encouraging, particularly since they were adversely affected by exchange rates and an increasingly weak insurance rating environment," Riley said.
Britain's third largest insurance broker, Sedgwick, also announced its plans on Tuesday to seek a listing on the New York Stock Exchange where it hopes to trade in June.
More than 40 percent of Sedgwick's business comes from North America.
It also plans a broader presence in southern Europe through its planned joint venture with Nikols, Italy's largest broker.
